name: Asana
one_liner: Work management platform for tasks, projects, and workspaces, with a REST API.
auth_notes: Personal access tokens and service account tokens are sent as Bearer tokens. OAuth is for apps where multiple users sign in. OpenID Connect is also documented.
access_notes: PATs are generated by the user in the developer console and are persistent by default. Service accounts are Enterprise-only and created by super admins. Cost is not stated in the cached pages. The community MCP README says the plan must allow API access.

buildability.rationale: PATs are self-serve and the REST API is documented. Cached pages do not confirm which plans allow API access. Service accounts are Enterprise-only, and multi-user apps need OAuth.

identity.quote: This is the interface for interacting with the Asana platform.

auth.quote: A personal access token (PAT) is the quickest and simplest way to authenticate in the API.
This is the best choice if multiple users need to sign in to your app.

access.quote: PATs are generated in the developer console.
Service Accounts are an Enterprise tier feature and can only be created by Asana super admins
Ensure the asana plan you have allows API access

api_surface.quote: The Asana API is a RESTful interface with predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts JSON or form-encoded requests, returns JSON, and uses standard HTTP features (verbs, response codes, etc.)

mcp.quote: This Model Context Protocol server implementation of Asana allows you to talk to Asana API from MCP Client

needs_human_reason: The cached pages do not state which plans include API access or what the API costs. Confirm plan eligibility before building.
